challenges.finding: Publisher reports insecurity and persistent threats against response teams in Tshopo (Bafwasende, Kabondo and Mangobo); threats from some local groups against response infrastructure at Mangote in the Beni health zone (Nord-Kivu); PoE/PoC out of service because of insecurity (Avakubi and Butuhe are named), strikes or late payment, and too few isolation facilities at ports and barriers, notably in Sud-Kivu; a strike by providers at the CTE in Kasenyi over unpaid wages and 14 patients not fed in the Mandima health zone (Ituri); a strike at Tchomia and input shortages at Mandima and Mambasa for decontamination; in Tshopo, 7 burial alerts with no safe burial carried out; a laboratory reagent stock-out (MVE buffer) with diesel running low for the incinerator and generator; and in Bas-Uele a calm situation but no guard shelters at secured sites, too little transport and no diesel in stock; and the vaccination section reports 195 vaccine doses at risk of expiry or loss. The Tshopo threats (SR173, SR180), the Avakubi closure (SR173 to SR177, SR179), the Butuhe closure (SR171, SR178 to SR180), the Kasenyi strike (SR171, SR173 to SR175, SR178, SR179), the Tchomia strike (SR179, SR180) and the Bas-Uele security and fuel lines (SR180) were printed before. No intervention effect is established.

Contact follow-up covers five reporting provinces. Sud-Ubangi prints ND and the Bas-Uele zero is withheld after the contact cohort moved between province labels in earlier editions. The lowest printed rate is Nord-Kivu (77.9%). No zero follow-up is inferred for any province.
